historical_claims.anchor: Published in 1953, Fahrenheit 451 belongs to a century marked by mass broadcasting, political conformity campaigns, book burnings, and new methods of entertainment.
The National Endowment for the Arts and the Library of Congress both place Bradbury's novel at the intersection of censorship and the growing influence of television.
Bradbury himself emphasized different dangers at different moments.

work.note: Existing survey chapter label '1953 · Fahrenheit 451' supplies the work's publication year; bibliography identifies the work. This dates publication, not its fictional setting or the lecture's creation.

description: Analyzes Fahrenheit 451 as a critique of censorship and spectacle, asking how television, social conformity, attention, and reading habits weaken a society’s capacity for thought.
